records.name: Gorontalo
records.summary:
The audited sources document Indonesia's national posture rather than Gorontalo: an October 2025 presidential decree lists "the promotion of LGBTQ+ culture" among non-military national-security threats alongside terrorism, radicalism and drug addiction; legal gender change requires sex-reassignment surgery plus judicial approval; a wave of vigilante mob attacks on trans women on 14-16 July 2026 - most severely more than fifteen people doused, stripped and beaten in Bogor, with footage circulated online - and researchers record markedly hardened anti-queer attitudes since 2016. Provincial moral enforcement is sharpest in Aceh, per the same feature.

Nothing in the audited material shows Gorontalo diverging in either direction: no documented local ordinance, raid wave, protection or service specific to the province. A visitor there is exposed to the national picture - identity not criminalised, visibility treated as a security threat, mob violence met with limited accountability.

records.name: Bengkulu
records.summary:
No Bengkulu-specific statute, enforcement action, protection or service appears in the audited sources; they establish the national frame a visitor shares here: a 2022 wire report (page unretrievable; fetch-time summary) on police denying mistreatment in the custody death of a foreign transgender activist on Bali, and an August 2026 feature on widening repression - the July 14-16 2026 vigilante wave against trans women (over fifteen doused, stripped and beaten in Bogor, filmed and shared), an October 2025 presidential decree naming "the promotion of LGBTQ+ culture" a non-military security threat, legal gender change conditioned on surgery plus judicial approval, and researchers' accounts of anti-queer attitudes hardening since 2016.

Bengkulu is therefore assessed on national conditions: no criminalisation of identity per se, official framing of visibility as a threat, and vigilante risk with weak accountability - without any documented local divergence in either direction.

records.name: Jambi
records.summary:
The audited sources contain no Jambi-specific finding; they set out the national framework that reaches visitors here: an October 2025 presidential decree listing "the promotion of LGBTQ+ culture" among non-military security threats; legal gender recognition conditioned on sex-reassignment surgery plus judicial approval; a July 14-16 2026 wave of vigilante mob attacks on trans women across the archipelago, concentrated in Bogor where more than fifteen people were doused, stripped and beaten on camera; and 2022 wire reporting, retrieved as a fetch-time summary, of police denying mistreatment after a foreign transgender activist died in Bali custody.

Researchers describe anti-queer attitudes hardening markedly since 2016. In Jambi, the risk profile is that national climate - official framing of visibility as subversive, mob violence with weak accountability, and no criminalisation of identity itself - with no documented local ordinance or protection either way.

records.name: Riau
records.summary:
Riau's audited sources are national-level: a 2022 wire report, retrieved only as a fetch-time summary, of police denying violence in the death in Bali custody of a transgender rights activist arrested on drug charges; and an August 2026 feature recording President Prabowo's October 2025 decree listing "the promotion of LGBTQ+ culture" among non-military security threats alongside terrorism and narcotics, and a wave of vigilante mob attacks on trans women during 14-16 July 2026, concentrated in West Java's Bogor, as the government moved to codify anti-LGBT attitudes into law.

No Riau-specific statute, raid, protection or service record appears in the material. The province is assessed under those national conditions: identity is not criminalised in most of the republic, but the official posture now treats visibility as a security threat and mob violence recurs with limited accountability; nothing documents a Riau divergence either way.

records.name: Maluku
records.summary:
Both audited sources for Maluku are national and were only partly retrievable: a 2022 wire report on police denying mistreatment in the death in Bali custody of a transgender activist arrested on drug charges (page not retrievable; fetch-time summary), and an August 2026 feature on widening repression of Indonesia's transgender community, including vigilante mob attacks (navigation-only at fetch; headline and dossier summary).

Neither source documents any Maluku-specific enforcement, ordinance, protection or service. The province is assessed on the national picture those sources sketch: criminalisation of same-sex conduct concentrated in the one province retaining religious courts, gender recognition restricted by surgery-plus-court rules, and an official and street-level hostility climate hardening since 2016 - asserted here only at the confidence the two hedged summaries support.
